### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the safety and order in mind. | # | Task | Key Points | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide purpose (gaming, workstation, general use).
• Set a budget (components + peripherals). | Use PCPartPicker to check compatibility and price alerts. | | 2 | **Gather Components** | • CPU, motherboard, RAM, GPU, storage (SSD/HDD), PSU, case, cooling (stock or aftermarket).
• Peripherals: monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers. | Stick to a single brand for the motherboard and CPU socket to avoid surprises. | | 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | • Clean, flat surface.
• Anti‑static wrist strap or mat.
• Screwdrivers (Phillips #0, #1). | Avoid carpet; static can damage components. | | 4 | **Install CPU** | • Open CPU socket latch.
• Align CPU (gold triangle) with socket.
• Gently place, lock latch. | Don’t force; check for bent pins. | | 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • Small pea‑size paste on CPU.
• Mount cooler (stock or aftermarket).
• Attach fan(s) to motherboard headers. | Use the cooler’s manual for torque specs. | | 6 | **Insert RAM** | • Open DIMM slots.
• Align notch, press until clicks. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel; follow motherboard manual. | | 7 | **Mount Motherboard in Case** | • Align standoffs with holes.
• Screw in place.
• Connect 24‑pin ATX, 8‑pin EPS power. | Keep cables tidy; use Velcro ties. | | 8 | **Install Storage** | • Mount SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot.
• Connect SATA data & power (if SATA). | Label cables for easier troubleshooting. | | 9 | **Install GPU** | • Insert into PCI‑e x16 slot.
• Secure with screws.
• Connect 6/8‑pin PCI‑e power. | Ensure slot is fully seated; use a small screwdriver to tighten. | | 10 | **Connect Power Supply** | • Mount PSU in case.
• Connect all cables: ATX, EPS, PCI‑e, SATA, 4‑pin CPU. | Use cable management to keep airflow. | | 11 | **Cable Management** | • Route cables behind motherboard tray.
• Use ties or Velcro straps. | Good airflow = better cooling. | | 12 | **Final Checks** | • Verify all connections.
• Ensure no loose screws or cables touching fans. | Double‑check power connectors. | | 13 | **Power On & BIOS** | • Connect monitor, keyboard, power button.
• Turn on.
• Enter BIOS (Del/F2).
• Check CPU, RAM, storage detected. | Update BIOS if needed. | | 14 | **Install Operating System** | • Create bootable USB (Windows 10/11, Ubuntu, etc.).
• Boot from USB, install OS. | Install drivers after OS installation. | | 15 | **Install Drivers & Software** | • GPU drivers (NVIDIA/AMD).
• Chipset drivers.
• Peripheral drivers. | Keep system updated. | | 16 | **Benchmark & Test** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor). | Ensure temperatures stay within safe limits. | | 17 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | • Keep dust‑free.
• Update drivers & BIOS periodically. | Clean fans every 3–6 months. | --- #### Quick Component Checklist | Category | Example Models (2026) | Notes | |----------|-----------------------|-------| | CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Intel Core i7‑14700K | Choose socket AM5 or LGA1700. | | Motherboard | ASUS ROG Strix B650E-F, MSI MPG Z790 Carbon Wi‑Fi | Ensure BIOS supports chosen CPU. | | RAM | Corsair Vengeance DDR5 32GB (2x16GB) | 6000MHz+ for gaming. | | GPU | NVIDIA RTX 4090, AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX | Check case clearance. | | Storage | Samsung 980 Pro 1TB NVMe | Fast boot & load times. | | PSU | Corsair RM850x 850W 80+ Gold | 80+ Gold for efficiency. | | Case | NZXT H710i, Fractal Design Meshify C | Good airflow, cable routing. | | Cooler | Noctua NH-D15, Corsair iCUE H150i | Air vs liquid depends on preference. | --- #### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **CPU not seated** | Re‑open socket, align correctly, lock latch. | | **RAM not recognized** | Install in correct slots, check BIOS. | | **GPU not detected** | Ensure PCI‑e slot is fully engaged, power cable connected. | | **No POST** | Check power connections, remove all peripherals, test with minimal components. | | **High temperatures** | Improve cable management, add case fans, reapply thermal paste. | --- #### Final Thought Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you control over performance, aesthetics, and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check each step, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
